questions.prompt: A cloned policy reaches 99% accuracy on held-out expert states yet fails often when run. What is the most likely reason?
options: Behaviour cloning cannot be used with neural network policies
The validation set is too small to give a reliable accuracy estimate
Its own small errors take it to states the demonstrations never covered
The expert was too good for the learner to imitate at all
questions.explanation: Held-out expert states measure error under the expert's state distribution. In closed loop the learner visits its own distribution.

questions.prompt: Per-step error 0.05 over 20 steps. Probability of at least one mistake? (three decimals)
questions.skillLabel: Compute the probability of a mistake

questions.prompt: Ditch model with eps = 0.02, no recovery (q = 0), T = 10. Expected steps off the demonstrated path? (two decimals)
In DAgger, who supplies the action labels for the states the learner visits?
options: A copy of the learner trained a step earlier
The learner itself, from its current policy
The expert, queried at the learner's states
questions.explanation: Self-labelling would reproduce the current policy. The point of DAgger is expert labels where the learner actually goes.

questions.prompt: Off-path recovery probability q = 0.18 per step and error eps = 0.02. Steady-state probability of being off the path eps/(eps+q)? (two decimals)
Explain why one-step accuracy on held-out expert data is not enough to judge a behaviour-cloned policy, and name the measurement that is.
rubric: Accuracy is measured under the expert's state distribution, not the learner's
Mistakes compound: a small error can lead to unseen states and failures
Measure closed-loop success over many rollouts with an interval
